facts.text: The only major-college player of the 2000s to make 150 threes: Stephen Curry, 2007-08 — 162 threes.
The only major-college player of the 2000s to score 800 points without making a three: Tyler Hansbrough, 2007-08 — 882 pts, 0 threes.
The only major-college player of the 2000s to record 100 blocks and 100 assists: Dominic McGuire, 2006-07 — 114 blk, 104 ast.
Only two major-college players of the 2000s made 300 free throws: Stefon Jackson (2008-09: 312-374 FT); Tyler Hansbrough (2007-08: 304-377 FT).
Only two major-college players of the 2000s recorded 130 steals: Desmond Cambridge (2001-02: 160 steals); John Linehan (2001-02: 139 steals).
Only two major-college teams of the 2000s made 400 threes as a team: VMI (2×, best 2006-07: 442 threes); Duke (2000-01: 407 threes).
Only two major-college players of the 2000s recorded 80 steals and 80 blocks: Damian Saunders (2009-10: 89 stl, 94 blk); Shane Battier (2000-01: 82 stl, 88 blk).
Only two major-college teams of the 2000s lost every game (15+ games): NJIT (2007-08: 0-29); Savannah St. (2004-05: 0-28).

Just four major-college teams of the 2000s averaged 90 points a game (15+ games): VMI (3×, best 2006-07: 100.9 ppg, 14-19); TCU (2000-01: 93.6 ppg, 20-11); Kansas (2001-02: 90.9 ppg, 33-4); Duke (2000-01: 90.7 ppg, 35-4).
Only two major-college players of the 2000s averaged 14 rebounds a game (15+ games): Blake Griffin (2008-09: 14.4 rpg); John Bryant (2008-09: 14.2 rpg).
Only two major-college players of the 2000s averaged 12 rebounds a game as a freshman (15+ games): Paul Millsap (2003-04: 12.5 rpg); Michael Beasley (2007-08: 12.4 rpg).

Just three major-college players of the 2000s averaged 25 points a game as a freshman (15+ games): Jason Conley (2001-02: 29.3 ppg); Michael Beasley (2007-08: 26.2 ppg); Kevin Durant (2006-07: 25.8 ppg).
Most 25-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 2000s: Keydren Clark, 3 (2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06).
Most 12-rebound-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 2000s: Paul Millsap, 3 (2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06).
Most 3-block-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 2000s: Deng Gai, 4 (2001-02, 2002-03, 2003-04, 2004-05).
Most 3-steal-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 2000s: Obie Trotter, 3 (2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06).
Most 100-three seasons in the 2000s: Keydren Clark, 4 (2002-03, 2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06).
Most 90-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 2000s: VMI, 3 (2006-07, 2007-08, 2008-09).

7 major-college players made 100 threes as a freshman in the 2000s. The most extreme: Stephen Curry, 2006-07 — 122 threes.

method: College basketball (men's): each line is one Stathead (Sports Reference college basketball) Season Finder query over the decade's ten seasons (a decade is the seasons starting in its years: the 1970s run 1970-71 to 1979-80), run in a signed-in subscriber session; result rows and stable ids are stored as provenance.

Sports Reference's season finders begin with 1947-48, so the 1940s page covers two seasons and earlier decades are not in the record. Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and the three-pointer (1986-87) arrive at different times; rules on a stat a season lacks return nothing. Per-game figures are totals divided by games.
